sources: WEDNESDAY Oct 21 2026 EARLY RUN (06:30 UTC, before the US open). US cash closes are TUESDAY Oct 20; oil, metals and FX carry live Wednesday European-session quotes. HEADLINE 1 - THE MISSING CREDIT PRINT LANDED, AND IT LANDED WIDE. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 finally posted the two sessions it owed: Oct 16 3.31 pct and Oct 19 3.29 pct (3.23 Oct 15, 3.25 Oct 14, 3.16 Oct 13, 3.11 Oct 12, 3.11 Oct 9). So the Friday rout DID widen credit, by 8bp on the day to 331bp, and only 2bp of that has come back. HY OAS is now 329bp versus the 323bp this board carried for three runs, plus roughly 18bp on the week and clearly outside the 303-312 band that held all through early October. This was the single most important missing number on the board and it resolved to the bad side. Trend up. HEADLINE 2 - EQUITY VOL KEEPS COLLAPSING AND THE OTHER DISCREPANCY RESOLVED THE OTHER WAY. FRED VIXCLS posted Oct 19 at 18.44, confirming the Yahoo figure and retiring the 18.07 value this board carried yesterday (so yesterday overstated the one-day drop). VIX then closed Oct 20 at 17.31, down a further 1.13 or minus 6.1 pct - a second consecutive fall and the lowest since Oct 15. Official path: 15.21 Oct 12, 15.27 Oct 13, 16.87 Oct 14, 16.46 Oct 15, 19.99 Oct 16, 18.44 Oct 19, 17.31 Oct 20. VIX is now only about 0.4 points above where it was a week ago, so the trend is reclassified from up to FLAT: the Oct 16 spike has essentially fully unwound in equity vol terms. Stocks held up (S and P 500 7,712.57 plus 0.28 pct, Nasdaq 26,424.82 minus 0.02 pct). HEADLINE 3 - OIL IS STILL THE PROBLEM. Brent is back near 110.4 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics Oct 21 serving 110.21-110.51, plus 1.3 to 1.6 pct on the day) after slipping on Tuesday. This is a third straight run with Brent at or above 110 and roughly 33 pct above pre-war levels. Fresh Red Sea and Gulf shipping risk plus threats to Saudi facilities continue to outweigh the Russian sanctions waiver and the Iranian Hormuz reopening offer, both of which remain on the table. Trend up and still the most important tile on the board. RATES: FRED T10Y2Y Oct 19 0.38 (0.35 Oct 16, 0.33 Oct 15, 0.37 Oct 14, 0.42 Oct 13) - the curve has steepened 5bp off last week's flat point and is now essentially unchanged on the week, so the trend is reclassified from down to FLAT. FRED has not yet posted Oct 20. The 10Y closed Oct 20 near 5.12 pct per cappnotes (down 3bp on their measure); note this does not reconcile cleanly with the 5.071 pct Investing close for Oct 19, so the 10Y level is uncertain by roughly 5bp this run - the SPREAD from FRED is the number used. FRED T5YIFR Oct 20 2.31 (2.31 and 2.33-2.34 through the prior week) - 5y5y breakevens are FLAT ON THE WEEK for a sixth consecutive run with Brent above 110. Still the most reassuring number on the board: the bond market continues to decline to price this oil shock as inflationary. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - CARRIED AND STALE FOR A SIXTH RUN: FRED NFCI is still at week ending Oct 9, minus 0.499. The post-selloff read releases TODAY Oct 21 at 12:30 UTC, which is AFTER this run, so it will be picked up tomorrow. This is now the most important pending number on the board, especially given the wide HY print. LABOUR - CARRIED: FRED ICSA week ending Oct 10 199k, fifth straight week in a 198-199k range, next release Oct 22. Labour remains the strongest tile. REAL ECONOMY - ONE GENUINE UPDATE: SEPTEMBER BUILDING PERMITS LANDED at 1,400k SAAR (Census and HUD, released Oct 20 12:30 UTC) versus a revised August 1,403k - essentially unchanged, so the tile is updated but the trend stays flat. Housing starts in the same release fell 5.2 pct to 1,221k and single-family permits fell about 4 pct, so the composition is softer than the headline permits number suggests, though Census notes the monthly change is not statistically significant. All other real-economy tiles carried: consumer sentiment 46.3 (UMich October preliminary, five-month low) trend down; ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next Nov 2); LEI y/y minus 0.7 pct (September release Oct 22); Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50). DOLLAR AND GROWTH PROXY: DXY 101.79 (Oct 20 close 101.71 minus 0.26 pct, Wednesday European session plus 0.08 pct) - down about 0.4 pct on the week and STILL refusing to rally on a third run of Brent above 110. Trend down. A dollar that will not bid in a supply shock remains the odd one out on this board. Growth proxy 1.59 for a second run (copper 6.56 USD/Lbs roughly flat at minus 0.06 pct, gold 4,117.52 USD/t.oz minus 0.17 pct and now DOWN FOUR STRAIGHT DAYS from 4,181; 6.56/4117.52*1000 = 1.593). The ratio is still rising only because gold is selling off, not because copper is rallying - mild risk-on, not a growth scare. Flat. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND, SIXTH RUN: the 3M SOFR-OIS spread was searched again and every free source serves the SOFR level or an OIS rate, never the spread, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is also CARRIED AS AN ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp - no free source publishes it. Global liquidity 1 (stable) is a judgement call: no balance-sheet regime change found for the Fed, ECB, PBOC or BOJ this run. Two assumed tiles and one judgement tile out of eighteen, unchanged for a sixth run. MOVE 101.30 Oct 19 (101.10 Oct 16, 102.49 Oct 15, 99.06 Oct 14, 101.09 Oct 13, 98.47 Oct 9) - no Oct 20 print on any free source; plus 2 pct on the week, flat. Rate vol has been remarkably well behaved throughout, hovering around 100 for two weeks. FED: Oct 27-28 FOMC, fed funds target 3.75-4.00 pct, hold remains the heavy consensus; no new pricing found this run. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy, working tree clean at start, no stale locks, this scheduled session remains the sole writer of data.json (GitHub Action disabled since Oct 17), BDTI stayed removed. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, SIXTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in plain text in .git/config. Fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Also still present: untracked junk in the repo root - _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/ - all safe to delete. PICTURE: the split board from yesterday is resolving, and not in the direction the equity market implies. The FINANCIAL side looks calmer on the surface - VIX has given back almost the entire Oct 16 spike, the curve has steepened back, rate vol is flat near 100, breakevens are flat at 2.31 for a sixth run, gold is down four days, claims are below 200k for a fifth week - but the one number that was missing has now landed wide: high yield spreads widened 8bp on the rout and have held 329bp, which is 18bp wider on the week and out of the band. Credit, not equity vol, is where the stress actually stuck. The PHYSICAL side continues to deteriorate with Brent above 110 for a third run. The honest read is that an AI-valuation wobble has mean-reverted in equity vol but left a real credit footprint, while a live oil shock grinds on and the bond market still refuses to call it inflationary. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: NFCI TODAY Oct 21 12:30 UTC, the first post-selloff financial conditions read and now the key number given the wide HY print; whether HY OAS keeps tightening back toward 312 or holds above 325; whether Brent holds above 110 or the Hormuz reopening is accepted; claims and September LEI Oct 22; EIA inventories today; the Oct 27-28 FOMC; rotating the embedded PAT.
